admission.justification: Realized across serving/held_reset_scheduler.py, cli/held_reset_delivery.py, and controlplane/held_store_layout.py, and guarded by unit-regression proofs in mcp/tests/test_held_reset_delivery.py.

applicability: Provider-limited recipients with a recorded reset timestamp whose reset time has passed.
conditions: deliver_due_pass snapshots index.due_at(now) and dispatches distinct recipients through a bounded pool (RESET_WORKERS = 16) via pool.map with buffersize=pool_size.
drain_reset_entry verifies receipt endpoints and delivers through drain_held and apply_drain_to_receipt in FIFO order.
Under D987 Option A, up to roughly 300 due recipients clear within about 30 seconds and larger simultaneous resets drain at about 11 recipients per second.
exclusions: Recipients whose host agent is archived, gone, closed without resume admission, in a non-steerable turn, or awaiting permission keep ordinary drain deferral or closure behavior.
statement: Every provider-limited recipient whose reset has passed is delivered in order through one bounded due pass rather than the ordinary rotating sweep: within about 30 seconds while up to about 300 recipients wait, and for a larger backlog at the host's measured rate of about 11 recipients a second (the physical witness measured 512 at 46.5 s).
title: Bounded post-reset held-message delivery pass
